prose_updates.tldr: Separate Brenier structure does not guarantee that a same-unit counterfactual composition preserves Euclidean ranks. The exact population frontiers and the robust counterexample to the published Euclidean implication are unconditional, as is the fixed-support Le Cam lower separation rate. The reported Hessians remain everywhere defined by clipping at \(m/4\); on the explicitly observed raw-Hessian event with \(r_{H,n}\le m/2\), clipping is inactive and the rank-margin interval and separated decisions are deterministically valid. A class-uniform probability bound for that event, the upper separation rate, and hence the matching two-sided frontier remain conditional on the complete endpoint-response, boundary-wavelet, extension-kernel, nonlinear-remainder, influence-kernel, increment, and concentration program stated in the conditional corollary. The eventual validated chord certificate retains its distinct stronger source-product trigger and is deterministic once the required band event and small-radius conditions hold.

project_justification.gap: Torous, Gunsilius, and Rigollet (2024), Section 3.1, Definition 1 and Theorem 2, identify a nonlinear difference-in-differences counterfactual law under cyclical comonotonicity, but do not give the symmetric-cross-Hessian Euclidean frontier, the Hessian-commutation cyclic-gradient frontier, the global margin, or inference for it. Ribeiro, Santhirasekaram, and Glocker's displayed dynamic-transport assumptions admit the audited open-neighborhood Brenier counterexample even though its symmetric cross-Hessian is indefinite. Existing statistical optimal-transport results provide integrated map risk or pointwise map limits, not a bounded-domain class-uniform raw-Hessian band. In particular, the cited response and elliptic papers do not supply the order-zero Hessian modulus, quantitative quadratic remainder, boundary-wavelet and extension-kernel implementation, or influence and concentration estimates needed for the matching upper frontier.
project_justification.niche: The delivered field-tier contribution is a graph-native common-rank Brenier counterfactual frontier: exact Euclidean and cyclic structural characterizations, an observable rank margin, a robust published-claim counterexample, an unconditional lower testing frontier, and a deterministic event-to-margin certificate. The class-uniform upper band and matching upper rate are isolated as a conditional program with every analytic and stochastic premise exposed.
project_justification.fill: The symmetric cross-Hessian theorem characterizes Euclidean monotonicity, the commutation theorem characterizes the cyclic-gradient subfamily, and the open-neighborhood matrices separate the full common-rank Brenier class from the stronger commuting subclass and refute the audited Euclidean implication under the displayed dynamic assumptions. The estimator uses a positive density fallback and \(m/4\) spectral clipping on every sample. The event-to-band theorem proves that, whenever \(\max_p\lVert\widetilde H_p-H_p\rVert_\infty\le r_{H,n}\le m/2\), clipping is inactive and all margin and threshold conclusions follow. A separate conditional corollary lists the endpoint-response, boundary-wavelet, extension-kernel, nonlinear-remainder, influence-kernel, increment, and Bernstein-net premises that would yield probability at least \(1-\delta\) and the selected upper rate. The matching-frontier proposition now invokes that corollary, while the fixed-support quadratic-bump mixture proves the lower rate independently. The validated certificate continues to use its distinct stronger source-product trigger.

sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Project each regime density at \(k_n\), use the strictly positive fallback off the computable regularity event, solve the normalized Monge--Ampere problem, smooth the potential at \(h_n\), form \(\widetilde H_p\), and clip spectrally at \(m/4\) before every inverse and margin statistic. Clipping is provably inactive on any raw-Hessian event satisfying \(r_{H,n}\le m/2\). Establishing that this event has class-uniform probability at least \(1-\delta\) requires all unresolved endpoint-response, boundary-wavelet, extension-kernel, nonlinear-remainder, influence-kernel, increment, and Bernstein-net estimates; it is neither a consequence of the deterministic band nor a model assumption.

prose_updates.related_work: De Lara and Ganassali (2025), Section 5.3, leave the cyclically monotone SCM characterization unresolved. Torous, Gunsilius, and Rigollet (2024), Section 3.1, Definition 1 and equation (6), define cyclical comonotonicity and show that it makes the relevant inverse composition cyclically monotone; their Theorem 2 uses that condition to identify a treated counterfactual law in nonlinear difference-in-differences. Their framework does not supply the pointwise symmetric-cross-Hessian Euclidean frontier, the Hessian-commutation cyclic-gradient frontier, the sharp global margin, or margin inference, and the common-rank Brenier framework does not claim their difference-in-differences identification result. Ribeiro, Santhirasekaram, and Glocker (NeurIPS 2025), Theorem 4.12 and Appendix Theorem B.11, assert strict Euclidean monotonicity under their displayed dynamic-transport conditions, but their proof uses a state-dependent weighted inner product; the audited open-neighborhood Brenier pair satisfies those displayed conditions while its Euclidean symmetric cross-Hessian is indefinite. Carlier, Chernozhukov, and Galichon (2016), Theorem 2.1, provide common-reference vector quantiles, not inverse-composition geometry. Hutter and Rigollet (2021) establish integrated map-risk rates. Manole et al. (2024) provide plug-in and boundary-wavelet machinery, and Manole et al. (2023) provide pointwise torus map limits, but neither source proves this bounded-domain simultaneous raw-Hessian band. Caja-Lopez, Delgadino, and Kitagawa (2026), Theorem 1.3, control \(C^{1,\alpha}\) potential error, while Theorem 1.5 gives a \(C^{2,\beta}\)-valued differentiable path and its conormal response; neither gives the class-uniform order-zero Hessian modulus or quantitative quadratic remainder required by the conditional program. Dong, Lee, and Kim (2020), Theorem 1.7, gives \(C^1\) regularity for a divergence-form conormal problem, whereas Theorem 1.10 concerns a different nondivergence oblique problem; neither furnishes the missing Hessian estimate. Their paper is in Indiana University Mathematics Journal 69(6), 1815--1853 (2020), DOI 10.1512/iumj.2020.69.8028. Ghosal and Sen (2022) study rank maps rather than cross-Hessian margins, and Chen and Fang (2019) motivate caution for ordinary bootstrap claims at degenerate nonsmooth functionals. None of these sources supplies the complete premise chain needed for the matching upper frontier or the validated source-product interval search; the latter's sufficient trigger remains distinct from the scalar margin endpoint except in the proved small-radius comparison.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The raw Hessian response is order zero and may accumulate a logarithm, while signed high-order smoothing need not preserve positive definiteness. Spectral clipping at \(m/4\) therefore totalizes the statistic. The proved deterministic theorem makes clipping inactive only on the explicitly defined event \(\mathcal B_n\) when \(r_{H,n}\le m/2\); it does not prove that event's probability. The conditional probability program still needs a uniform boundary-wavelet projection, a bounded polynomial-reproducing extension kernel, the endpoint linearization and quadratic remainder, influence-kernel variance and envelope bounds, an increment bound, and matrix-Bernstein/net concentration. Consequently the matching upper frontier cannot be routed through the deterministic event-to-band theorem alone. The finite certificate additionally uses a source-product allowance \((2M+r_{H,n})r_{H,n}t_{\mathrm{ch}}^2\lVert z\rVert_2^2\), and its trigger is not equivalent to the scalar margin trigger at arbitrary radii. Validated interval arithmetic remains necessary, and the lower bound retains its strict-slack nondegeneracy qualification.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The exact Euclidean and cyclic structural frontiers, the NeurIPS-assumption-aligned open-neighborhood witness, the deterministic event-to-margin theorem, the explicit fixed-support Le Cam lower family, and the small-radius validated-certificate implication are proved components. The boundary-uniform Hessian endpoint modulus, quantitative quadratic remainder, boundary-wavelet and extension-kernel construction, and influence, increment, and concentration chain are open; none is supplied by the cited sources. Accordingly, class-uniform coverage, the upper separation rate, and a matching two-sided testing frontier are conditional on every premise explicitly listed in \(\mathrm{prop:conditional\text{-}uniform\text{-}margin\text{-}band}\), whereas the lower separation rate is unconditional relative to that program under its strict-slack qualification. The certificate's source-product trigger is a distinct stronger sufficient condition, with no arbitrary-radius equivalence to the scalar negative-margin endpoint and no termination claim at zero margin. No adaptation, irregular-support, coordinate-invariance, unvalidated-numerics, or empirical-violation claim is made. The scalar and simultaneously diagonal cases still reduce to positive derivative ratios.
